name: Foxfire
manufacturer: Cultivar collective known as 'The Garden', Gary Ruins
description: A liquid extract brewed from genetically-drifted bioluminescent fungi cultivated in the flooded basement levels of the Gary Ruins — fungi that have been growing in contact with leached geneware runoff for decades and have mutated into something novel. The brew causes vivid phosphene hallucinations, a feeling of bodily warmth, and in some users, temporary bioluminescence of the skin and mucous membranes. The Garden treats it as a sacrament. Everyone else treats it as the cheapest trip available.
effects: intense visual hallucinations with luminescent quality
profound sense of bodily warmth and connectedness
temporary skin bioluminescence in ~30% of users
side_effects: in rare cases, bioluminescence becomes permanent
fungal spore inhalation risk if brew is improperly sealed
psychotic breaks in users with latent neurological conditions
cultural_context: The Garden is a genuine subculture in the Gary Ruins — they've been cultivating their fungi for thirty years and view Foxfire as a spiritual tool. They sell excess product only reluctantly, and there are counterfeit batches made by opportunists that have caused deaths. True Garden-brewed Foxfire comes in hand-sealed clay bottles with a thumbprint in the wax. The glowing skin effect has made it fashionable in certain underground art scenes.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 biotech researcher has quietly identified that the Gary fungi have developed genuinely novel enzymatic properties — someone powerful wants The Garden's location and cultivation methods, and they're not asking nicely
A user's permanent bioluminescence is spreading — it's not just cosmetic anymore, and it's attracting attention from Helix Biosystems
The Garden's eldest cultivar has died, and a succession dispute is fracturing the collective — someone needs to broker peace before the knowledge of proper cultivation dies with the conflict
